Greetings,

When running recordTable with the following call I get the warning "omitting X images because of missing/unreadable date/time information":

recordtable<- recordTable(inDir = "E:/2018_tagged",
                        IDfrom = "metadata",
                        camerasIndependent = T,
                        minDeltaTime = 1,
                        deltaTimeComparedTo = "lastRecord",
                        metadataSpeciesTag = "Species",
                        timeZone = "America/Los_Angeles")

Warning: 14 : omitting 2 images because of missing/unreadable date/time information.

The warnings only happen for certain folders. For the purposes of troubleshooting, is there a way to find out which images were omitted?

Or better yet, is there a solution for this?

Please let me know if more information is needed.

Thank you,
Joel

messages.subject: Solar time
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

It's intuitive to convert from clock time to solar time when assessing diel activity.
There are a few r packages to do this (e.g. The solaR R package by Oscar Perpiñán Lamigueiro), but I was wandering, before I dive into this, if anyone had some code (that they would be willing to share) to directly convert a camtrapr record table to solar time? Or even recommendations about the best way to go about this?

Cheers,
Matt.

messages.subject: Re: Solar time
messages.body_plain:
Matt

We have done a lot of work here but ...  As an exercise we are replicating Ikeda et al's paper. I am just discussing with my brother (my R guru) what we did and why.

My thinking is -
assign the time zone to GTM+10 (or -10 - I get muddled and have to check).  That solves the discontinuity with Australia daylight saving.
we have done the analysis of diel activity on this time zone.
for every record my brother calculated dawn and dusk (with an R package) and arbitrarily defined
       dawn twilight plus-minus 1 hour of sunrise
       dusk twilight plus-minus 1 hour of sunset
my brother plotted a ggplot version of the diel activity (with confidence intervals)
       there is some discussion to be had on how we test for difference
(we also looked at what was an independent record).

We are open to discussion or correction but my first thought is that adjusting for difference in sunrise-sunset across a 600  Squ km study area is overkill. If you did that you might need to correct for topography - especially in the Otway Ranges but unnecessary for Western Port 'plains'.  Using solar time for each location of each image and differentiating between - for example noon (mid way between dawn and dusk) verses the time of the sun's highest point in the sky might again be overkill.

These are my musings.

I'd welcome help finding reviews or references defining and applying definitions of crepuscular, cathermeral to real mammals.  I don't have easy access to the literature.
regards
David

messages.body_plain:
Dear Bernat,
my apologies for the late response. Currently there is no such function available in the package.
surveyReport can give you the number of records by species and station, but not by day.

But as this is a recurring question I played around with detectionHistory a little and may have found a solution, see attachment. I didn't test it properly, so please be careful and treat it as experimental code for the moment. I might include it in the next version, but then incorporated into detectionHistory.

The function is called detectionHistory_sum and works just like detectionHistory, but it returns counts instead of the binary 1/0. In order to run it you need to run the other script, variousOtherHelperFunctions. Not all of its content is needed, but it is most convenient to just run or source the whole thing.

Again, please be aware, this is only a temporary fix at best. And let us know if it works please.

All the best,
Jürgen

messages.body_plain:
Hi Joel,
the function does not return this information. It might be a good idea to add that. The function tells you that the problem is in station 14 though.

In the meantime, maybe digiKam or some other image viewer/editor can help? In digikam see the left side, the Dates or Timeline menus.

Alternatively, use the terminal (cmd.exe) and run exiftool directly on that folder:

exiftool -EXIF:DateTimeOriginal E:/2018_tagged/14

The 14 is just a guess about your folder name. Replace the path with whatever it is on your hard disk,

You should be able to spot which one is the cuprit (it may be a hassle though with many images).

Cheers,
Jürgen
